texts:
If you have an avatar file and nowhere left to use it, bring it here. Paste its link or upload the .glb or .vrm, and it is saved to your account, mapped onto our animation library, and ready to put on a website with two lines of HTML.

three.ws/import/rpm

Finding the file: if an app loaded your avatar from a link, open your browser's developer tools, go to the Network tab, filter by .glb or .vrm, and copy the request URL. If you saved the file earlier, use the Upload File tab instead.

Whatever rig it came with, its bone names are mapped onto one canonical skeleton, so the idle and walk clips play on it. VRM 0.x and 1.0 files keep their toon shading, spring-bone hair and cloth, and expressions, and voice or camera capture can drive the face.

Then give it a job. Make it an agent with its own page and a Solana wallet, or put it on your own site with <agent-3d body="my-avatar.glb" brain="free"> and it talks to visitors with no API key. The embed guide: three.ws/docs/embedding

issues.quote: If you have an avatar file and nowhere left to use it, bring it here.
issues.problem: The head post does not open with the mechanism or the strongest true statement as required by the house voice contract. It leads with a conditional invitation instead of stating what the feature does.
issues.fix: Replace the opening with a mechanism lead: Paste a .glb or .vrm avatar link or upload the file, and three.ws saves it to your account, maps its bones onto one canonical skeleton, and makes it embeddable with two lines of HTML.

issues.problem: The house voice contract requires linking the surface once, one link to the page the post is about. The thread contains two links (import page in post 1, embed guide in post 4).
issues.fix: Remove the embed guide link from post 4 and keep only three.ws/import/rpm in the head post.
